findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed facility to be using quaternary ammonium sanitizer, but facility only had test strips for chlorine sanitizers. Discussed what strips to buy and where to get them with PIC. These strips can be purchased from food distributors or online. The strips will be for measuring the concentration of quaternary ammonium concentrations. They’re commonly called QAC strips. They come in rolls and also individual sticks. Inspector will return 09/22/2025 to check if facility has gotten the strips.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.comment:
A certified food protection manager is required to be on-site during hours of operation.  The CFM was not present at the facility at the time of inspection.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

(REPEAT) Facility uses regular household sponges (magic eraser) for the wiping down of roller bars and counter cleanup. PIC advised to cease this behavior immediately as sponges tend to sit out in ambient air and accumulate bacteria over time, when sponges are used all throughout those pathogens are being spread all over the establishment.  Inspector will follow up to see that acceptable sanitizer bucket and/or spray is in use for countertop cleanup and that alternative materials are used for warewashing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
-(REPEAT) Ice machine was observed to contain a build-up of mold/debris.  Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch.  Ensure ice machine is cleaned and sanitized regularly to prevent build up of mold/debris, contaminating ice.
-(REPEAT) Ice scoop was observed to be stored in ice machine with handle in contact with ice.  Ice scoop handle is in direct contact with ice, causing contamination of ice.  Ensure ice scoop is stored with the handle up and out of ice.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer was prepared at time of inspection, although food preparation and cooking had occurred.  Sanitizer shall be available during hours of operation to clean food contact surfaces and to prevent food contamination.  Ensure a sanitizer bucket is made and available during all hours of operation.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements.

Bleach located under 2-compartment sink lacked EPA labeling information, and specifications for use on food contact surfaces. Inspector went over labeling requirements with PIC and advised to purchase appropriate bleach for food service (and associated strips see #48). After inspection was concluded, PIC located a bottle of bleach elsewhere in facility that contained an EPA label, directions for ppm use on food contact surfaces. Inspector advised the improper bleach be relocated to a janitorial closet or similar location so it is not used accidentally in the food preparation sites.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

Facility uses regular household sponges for all warewashing, wiping down of roller bars, and counter cleanup. PIC advised to cease this behavior immediately as sponges tend to sit out in ambient air and accumulate bacteria over time, when sponges are used all throughout (especially with no sanitizing step) those pathogens are being spread all over the establishment. Inspector will follow up to see that acceptable sanitizer bucket and/or spray is in use for countertop cleanup and that alternative materials are used for warewashing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

See item #1. A single 2-compartment sink is being utilized for all purposes: warewashing, dumping of guest coolers, dumping of food, and handwashing. Inspector provided education that this behavior is unacceptable, presents a contamination risk, and handwashing needs to occur in its own designated handwashing sink. Will follow up to see that this behavior ceases.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

PIC does not appear to demonstrate knowledge about importance of using designated handsinks to prevent contamination. PIC was asked where warewashing occurs, he gestured towards the 2-part sink where he had previously stated handwashing occurs. When inspector asked about their process for warewashing he stated they use a sponge and Dawn dish soap to wash tongs for hot dogs and roller bars for hot dogs. When inspector asked if these items are sanitized at all, he did not appear to understand what inspector was asking and stated the items are not sanitized they are just washed with Dawn. Inspector asked about sanitizing agents present within facility and stated there is bleach under the sink (see 28). The bleach did not meet labeling requirements. Test strips were not present. PIC then asked if sanitizing hand wipes would be sufficient to sanitize roller bars for hot dogs. 

Inspector discussed these key food safety items with PIC and stated that handwashing must occur in a designated sink only and all other washing/rinsing/dumping must occur elsewhere. Discussed proper labeling requirements and use/application of sanitizers in a food establishment. Provided education on changes needed within facility and set a follow up date of 7/29.
